parts:
Hi fellow Nimble users,

I don't have much experience in Nimble, I did several models before, however, right now I am stuck with a particular error and hope that you can help me solve it.

I am doing a continuous time-varying CJS model to estimate survival and recapture probabilities. The model I am doing right now is checking the effects of forklength. 
Model in a nutshell:
 Survival model: logit(phi[i,t]) <- alpha1 + beta1*forklength[i,t]
 Recapture model: logit(p[i,t]) <- alpha2 + beta2*forklength[i,t]

Fork length is unknown when the individuals are not captured. 

Now I am getting this error when I try to run the model,
[Note] Infinite values were detected in model variable: logProb_y.

And then after compiling I also get a lot of lines of this error:
...
warning: logProb of data node y[5, 2]: logProb is -Inf. warning: logProb of data node y[8, 2]: logProb is -Inf. warning: logProb of data node y[10, 2]: logProb is -Inf. warning: logProb of data node y[12, 2]: logProb is -Inf. warning: logProb of data node y[14, 2]: logProb is -Inf. warning: logProb of data node y[1, 4]: logProb is -Inf.
I'd appreciate it if anyone has any idea on how to solve this. I am attaching the model code and a sample dataset to replicate the error.
Thanks in advance!
Arjun

messages.author: 7878556d408ec9ec
messages.subject: Re: Error "Infinite values were detected in model variables: logProb_y
parts:
Hi Arjun,

In your model, the node y[5,2] (and similar for others appearing in the warning message) takes value 1 while the probability vector used for declaring the node ( y[i, t] ~ dcat(po[z[i, t], 1:2, i, t])) always takes (0, 1) in MCMC sampling. It seems when updating the values of alpha and beta (not very big variation), the probability vector does not move away from (0, 1) and thus causes the -Inf logProb warning. It seems that your fl variable takes big values and these lead to the value 1 for phi and p in the short MCMC run (which gives you (0,1) for the probability vector for dcat). It might help to get MCMC to move from the stuck point if you choose better starting values..   

Best wishes,
Wei

messages.subject: Re: Error "Infinite values were detected in model variables: logProb_y
parts:
Hi Arjun,

I agree with Wei on his point. However, finding the appropriate starting values that work seems hard.

What you could do is to scale your covariates (fl) that you are passing into the logit function, they don't necessarily need to be between 0 and 1 but must be small. For example, use this in the data-init list section: 

new_fl <- scale(fl)[,1]

If you have some missing values NA, they will be returned as NA. Then, pass the new_covariate into either your data list like this.

my.data = list(y=y + 1, fl = new_fl)     # I got this from your code but instead replace fl with new_fl which is a scaled fl.

Let me know if it works for you.

Thank you.

Your friend 

Kenny.

Arjun, the way you set up the data and missing values is fine. The thing that does not make sense is explained in more detail below. 

In your simulated fl data, the 1st row is:  NA, 174, 181, NA, 182, NA ,188. This means the 1st individual is first captured on the 2nd occasion. So, we need to model the observed difference between the 2nd and 3rd occasions, i.e. 7 (=181-174), using the gamma distribution. Then we need to use delta[1, 1] ~ dgamma(a, b) for the difference between the 3rd and 4th occasions, and let the missing fl[1, 4] <- fl[1, 3] + delta[1, 1]. Now we need to model the next revolution, i.e. fl[1,5] - fl[1,4] using the gamma dist. Next is delta[1,2] ~ dgamma(a, b) for the missing value on occasion 6, etc. The annoying thing is that we cannot declare something like fl[1, 5] - fl[1, 4] ~ dgamma(a, b) in nimble model code. I may be wrong but I do not have a better way to handle this than the following two:

1. You can write a custom distribution like this:

dFL <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(x = double(), # current value
                 prevFL = double(), # previous value
                 shape = double(),
                 scale = double(),
                 log = integer(0, default = 0)) {
    logProb <- dgamma(x - prevFL, shape, scale, log = TRUE)
    if (log) return(logProb)
    else return(exp(logProb))
    returnType(double())
  }
)

and then use it in your model code like this:

for(t in (first[i]+1):nyears){
      fl[i, t] ~ dFL(fl[i, t-1], a, b)
}

2. Maybe something like this using a normal distribution for the revolution of the covariate

for(t in (first[i]+1):nyears){
      fl[i, t] ~ dnorm(fl[i, t-1] + mu[t], sd = sigma)
}

Let me know if anything helps. 

Best wishes,
Wei
